problem: Embodied agents are mostly episodic and start each episode with an empty memory. Transformers with attention over the history cost O(N^2) to query, and classical RNNs couple memory capacity to network capacity quadratically, so neither suits long-term continuous robot operation.
motivation: Real robots should use observations gathered before an episode starts (e.g., a prior exploration) to find their bearings and reach goals efficiently. That needs a compact, scalable, O(1) recurrent memory that can be queried with an image for relative pose.
key_idea: Kinaema keeps a distributed latent memory of N embeddings, updated recurrently by a self-attention transformer followed by a weight-shared GRU gate. It is pre-trained on Mem-RPE (relative pose between a query image and memory), plus masked image modeling, and then plugged into an RL ImageNav agent.
insight: Both the transformer update and the gating are needed: removing either drops Mem-RPE (1m/10° accuracy at T=200) from 24 to 11. Fewer, larger embeddings work better at a fixed total memory size (20x3.1k gives 24/52/77 vs 160x384 giving 4/19/44). Randomizing training sequence length and adding masked image modeling are key for generalizing to longer sequences (T=800: 13 vs 4). Naively injecting the priming sequence into the agent's hidden state hurts, while a dedicated memory plus pose decoder helps.
method: Recurrent distributed memory: state h_t is N=20 embeddings of dim 3072, updated per step from a DINOv2 ViT-S/14 image embedding and an odometry MLP embedding.

Correction + transformer update: a per-embedding linear layer combines h_{t-1}+learned positional embedding with the observation, then a 3-layer self-attention transformer contextualizes the embeddings.
Gating: a weight-shared GRU cell (3 layers) applied per embedding blends old state and update candidates for stability, which decouples memory capacity from gating cost.

Read-out and RPE decoder: the memory is reshaped (20x3072 to 160x384) and a cross-attention decoder with the query image as Q, followed by self-attention and a CLS-token MLP, predicts distance, bearing and rotation.
Mem-RPE pre-training: L1 pose loss on the observed and alternative unseen-but-nearby images, with random sequence lengths 50–100, plus an auxiliary masked image modeling head.

Mem-Nav agent: a DEBiT-B agent is extended by feeding the penultimate-layer latent of Kinaema's goal-pose estimate into the agent GRU (zero-initialized weights). It is fine-tuned with PPO on HM3D episodes with priming sequences of about 200 steps.

setting.backbone: Kinaema (DINOv2 ViT-S/14 encoder + transformer/GRU recurrent memory) plus a DEBiT-B RL agent (ResNet-18, binocular transformer, GRU), trained
setting.training_data: Mem-RPE: 80M frames from 800 HM3D train scenes (100k per scene), with alternative-camera frames; Mem-Nav: 8M episodes on HM3D train (10k per scene) with pre-generated priming cycles. The agent is initialized from the DEBiT-B checkpoint and fine-tuned with PPO for 100M steps (the method section says 300M).
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 112x112 + odometry (7-D pose difference) + goal image; priming sequence of ~200 steps before the episode
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10°, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (odometry is given; the priming path is predefined, not chosen by the agent)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark numbers; Mem-Nav is the paper's own task and only SPL is reported (no SR table), in bins by goal distance and primer seen/unseen. Success rates appear only in figures, if at all.
results: On Mem-RPE, Kinaema beats GRU, xLSTM, EMA, LRU, MooG and Trunc.Hist., especially on longer sequences (T=800: 10/21/37 vs GRU 4/14/31). On Mem-Nav, with a primer it gets the best SPL in most bins (e.g. HARD seen 54 vs DEBiT finetune 48 and GRU memory 50), and the priming sequence adds up to +10 SPL. Gains over the DEBiT and GRU-memory agents are modest, often 1–4 SPL.
limitations: Does not estimate whether the goal was seen before; training is limited to T=100 steps, and the single-embedding-per-image input may limit future gains.
Kinaema training is bimodal across seeds (either excellent or mediocre), and the RL fine-tuning is very expensive (~30 days on an H100).
Mem-Nav navigation gains over the strong DEBiT and GRU-memory baselines are modest, without error bars or seeds; the GRU read-out ablations were lost.
